multibyte.label: The message line that never ended
multibyte.explanation: The screen row holds eighty characters, one of them two bytes wide, so the text needs eighty-one bytes plus its terminator - one byte past the wide-count limit the conversion used. The original truncates exactly at the limit and writes no terminator, and the caller measures the buffer as a string: with the buffer junked and no zero anywhere, the measurement runs through all thousand twenty-four stale bytes. The correction bounds the conversion by the widest encoding for the same character count, so the full text converts and terminates at eighty-one.

control.label: Control: a pure-ASCII row
control.explanation: The same row with every character one byte wide fits the old limit too: both variants terminate identically at eighty, and the complete log is byte-identical.
